Treasury curve used for pricing

Par yields converted to continuous rates, interpolated linearly to each expiration. Illustrative values, not a live feed.

Methods

IV is solved from each mid with the native model: Bjerksund-Stensland 2002 for American equity/ETF options, Black-Scholes-Merton for European index options. No bid, no IV.

Theo prices off the fitted surface, not the option’s own IV, so theo minus mid shows where the quote sits. CRR uses 100 steps.

30-day IV applies the Cboe VIX method to each chain (forward from the ATM call–put mid, strips cut after two zero bids, minute-weighted interpolation across 30 days). One-day move = spot × 30-day IV × √(1/252). With earnings inside 7 days, the move to the first post-earnings expiration and the implied event move from the two post-earnings expirations are added.

IV shock (chain only) changes Theo and the chain greeks. Parallel and proportional methods move every vol by the same points or percentage. The normalized-strike method raises the ATM vol and keeps the skew fixed as a vol-point spread over ATM in normalized strikes z = ln(K/F)/(σATM√T); each strike takes the skew at its new z, so a downward skew flattens as vol rises. √time scaling multiplies the shock by √(30/days to expiry).

P&L is unrealized against cost basis at mid marks; there is no prior-close price in the sample data, so no day P&L yet.

Requirements are Reg T initial and FINRA 4210 maintenance minimums. Pairing sequence: conversions/reversals, collars, covered, protective, boxes, iron condors, butterflies, verticals, calendars/diagonals, short combos, naked; the largest naked requirement is paired first within each step.
